bodyHtml:
What results have FocusedEDU's school partners measured?

FocusedEDU has published measured results from 4 school partners, and each one is named below. The results run from 120+ placements across one school to 100% of open special education teacher roles filled within 2 weeks at 2 others. Every figure in the table comes from that school's published case study.

SchoolLocationPartner sinceWhat they neededWhat was measured
Odyssey Public Charter SchoolWilmington, DE2021Substitute and certified teachers, SLPs, OTs, PTs, psychologists, reading specialists, 1:1 aides, paraprofessionals, bus drivers and support rolesPlacements across the school: 120+. Day-to-day substitute fill rate: 95%. Improvement over the previous provider: 40%+. Distinct role types filled: 13+.
IDEA Public Charter SchoolWashington, DC2022Certified special education teachers, substitute teachers and 1:1 aidesOpen certified special education teacher roles filled: 100%. Retention of the educators placed: 100%. Time from request to filled: 2 weeks.
Cesar Chavez Public Charter SchoolWashington, DC2022Dedicated aides, special education teachers, subject-certified long-term substitutes and related support rolesQualified candidates presented per opening: 4, on average. Role types available: 13+.
First Philadelphia Public Charter SchoolPhiladelphia, PA2021Certified special education teachers, paraprofessionals, substitute teachers and 1:1 aidesRetention of the special education teachers placed: 100%. Open special education teacher roles filled: 100%. Time from request to filled: 2 weeks.

Two more results are published on FocusedEDU's home page without the partner's name. One partner reached a vacancy rate under 10%, down from 35%. A partner district measured a +25% lift in its substitute fill rate.

Two of the partnerships began in 2021 and 2 began in 2022. FocusedEDU has spent 12 years partnering with K-12 schools, and the full write-ups are on the case studies page.

What happened at each of the 4 schools?

Each school came to FocusedEDU with open roles that traditional recruiting had not filled, in a limited local talent pool. Each got recruiting built around that one school, and each kept the hiring decision.

How did Odyssey Public Charter School fill 120+ roles?

The challenge. Odyssey serves more than 1,000 K-8 students drawn from 5 districts, with a 12:1 student-teacher ratio to protect. Traditional recruiting fell short, and the staffing agencies already under contract couldn't fill the open roles. The gaps ran across the whole building: substitute and classroom teachers, SLPs, OTs and PTs, psychologists, reading specialists, 1:1 aides, paraprofessionals, bus drivers and support roles.

What was done. FocusedEDU built one dependable pipeline across every role type. Each candidate was sourced, interviewed, credentialed and reference-checked before a vetted shortlist went to the school for its final decision. A customized recruiting plan of digital advertising, on-location information sessions and grassroots outreach built a talent pool deep enough to keep day-to-day coverage reliable.

  • Placements: 120+ across the school, from bus drivers and certified teachers to paraprofessionals and substitutes.
  • Substitute coverage: a 95% fill rate on day-to-day substitutes, a 40%+ improvement over the previous provider.
  • Range: one partner covering 13+ distinct roles.
  • Length: trusted and renewed as a partner since 2021.

Read the full Odyssey Public Charter School case study. How daily coverage is built is on our substitute teacher staffing page.

How did IDEA Public Charter School fill every special education teacher role?

The challenge. IDEA PCS in Washington, DC was short on special education teachers, substitutes and 1:1 aides, and it was fighting an uphill reputation in the local talent market. A limited candidate pool and a soft employer brand meant traditional recruiting stalled. The agencies already on contract had not changed that.

What was done. FocusedEDU built a recruiting plan designed to change the narrative around IDEA: digital and grassroots advertising, on-site information sessions, and a campaign built around the real, positive experiences of the contractors placed there. Satisfied educators told the story, and the perception of IDEA as a place to work shifted.

  • Roles filled: 100% of open certified special education teacher roles.
  • Retention: 100% of the educators placed.
  • Speed: every role filled within 2 weeks of the request.
  • Length: a partnership that has held since 2022.

Read the full IDEA Public Charter School case study.

How did Cesar Chavez Public Charter School get 4 candidates for every opening?

The challenge. Cesar Chavez PCS runs a rigorous college-prep program and a distinctive public-policy curriculum for 414 students in grades 6 to 12 in Northeast DC. A thin local talent pool left the school short on dedicated aides, special education teachers and subject-certified long-term substitutes, and conventional recruiting couldn't keep pace.

What was done. FocusedEDU built a dedicated pipeline for Chavez and sourced deep, presenting on average 4 qualified candidates for every open position. FocusedEDU handled the advertising, interviewing, credentialing and screening, then put a vetted shortlist in front of the school. The final call was always the school's.

  • Choice: 4 qualified candidates presented per opening.
  • Fit: specialized roles filled to the school's standard, including dedicated aides, special education teachers and subject-certified long-term substitutes.
  • Consistency: a repeatable pipeline the school can count on.

Read the full Cesar Chavez Public Charter School case study.

How did First Philadelphia Public Charter School keep every special education teacher placed?

The challenge. First Philadelphia needed its most difficult roles filled: certified special education teachers, paraprofessionals, substitutes and 1:1 aides. These are the positions where a vacancy lands directly on the students who can least afford it. A limited local talent pool and traditional recruiting methods weren't keeping up.

What was done. Working directly with the school's leadership, FocusedEDU built a customized recruiting plan and a dedicated pipeline, and consistently presented multiple qualified candidates per position so the school could choose the right fit. FocusedEDU owned the advertising, interviewing, credentialing and screening end to end, and stayed focused on the special education roles where continuity matters most.

  • Retention: 100%. Every certified special education teacher placed stayed, giving students unbroken support.
  • Roles filled: 100% of open special education teacher roles, each one within 2 weeks of the request.
  • Choice: multiple vetted candidates presented per opening.
  • Length: a partnership that has held since 2021.

Read the full First Philadelphia Public Charter School case study.

Why do results on special education roles carry the most weight?

Special education seats are the hardest teaching positions to fill, by the federal government's own count. Two of the 4 case studies measure exactly those seats, and both report every open special education teacher role filled within 2 weeks.

Before the 2024-25 school year, 74% of elementary schools and 74% of middle schools with a special education vacancy reported difficulty filling it with a fully certified teacher. Public schools filled 77% of their special education vacancies with fully certified teachers before classes started. The NCES commissioner said special education positions "remain the most difficult to fill" (source: NCES School Pulse Panel, October 17, 2024 release). In October 2024, 34% of public school leaders said they felt understaffed in special education (source: NCES School Pulse Panel, December 12, 2024 release).

That is the market IDEA Public Charter School and First Philadelphia Public Charter School were hiring in. Both had 100% of their open special education teacher roles filled, and both kept the educators placed. Role detail is on our special education staffing page.

The seat costs your district every week it stays open. The arithmetic is in what an unfilled classroom costs a school district, and the service obligations that keep running during a vacancy are covered in managing IEP backlogs and compensatory services.

What do school leaders say in their signed letters?

Eight school leaders have signed letters of recommendation, from superintendents, principals and HR directors at partner schools across New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware and Colorado. Every sentence quoted below is in the signed letter, and every letter is downloadable in full from the references page.

  • Lennita Porter-Linen, BHRM, MAEL, Director of Human Resources Recruitment and Retention, Bridgeton Public Schools (Bridgeton, NJ), June 2026. "I recommend Focused Staffing Group without reservation." Her letter says the firm "has presented several qualified educator candidates who have contributed positively to our instructional environment and student experience."
  • Elias Pappas, CEO, Odyssey Charter School (Wilmington, DE), March 2024. "One of the hallmarks of our collaboration with Focused Staffing Group is their innovative temp-to-perm clause, which has allowed Odyssey Charter School to assess the suitability of referred professionals before making permanent hiring decisions, all at no cost to the school."
  • Kelly Hamm, Human Resources Director, Lotus School for Excellence (Aurora, CO), October 2024. The school used temp-to-perm to fill what her letter calls "a highly specialized and hard-to-fill Special Education Coordinator position." She wrote: "From the very beginning, your team has been consistently communicative, ensuring that we are kept informed at every stage of the process." On moving that coordinator to permanent status, the school was "thrilled that we can do so without a buyout fee."
  • Erin D. Murphy-Richardson, Superintendent, The Barack Obama Green Charter Schools (Plainfield, NJ), March 2024. "Focused Staffing Group has consistently matched us with exceptional talent who have made a significant impact on our students' learning experience." And: "The quality of the candidates they have sourced for us has been nothing short of exceptional."
  • David Weathington, MSW, LSW, Ed.D, CEO, Buttonwood Farms / Delta School (Philadelphia, PA), February 2024. "Overall, Focused Staffing Group has been an invaluable partner in ensuring the continuity of education in our school." The letter covers special education teachers, paraprofessionals, personal care assistants and related service providers.
  • Zavia Herring, Director of Human Resources, Renaissance Academy Charter School (Phoenixville, PA), March 2024. "They have always been quick to respond to our staffing needs, often providing us with suitable candidates at short notice."
  • Dr. Heather Brooks, Principal, Serviam Girls Academy (New Castle, DE), May 2025. The school filled 2 middle school positions, a math teacher and a PE/health teacher. "Their responsiveness helped us move quickly through each phase of hiring, ensuring that our students had qualified teachers in place without delay."
  • Tracy H. Foedisch, Hiring & Support Manager, Hope Community Charter School (Camden, NJ), March 2024. The letter describes 3 professionals working at the school, in social work, speech and language, and school administration. "They are all very experienced and knowledgeable in their respective fields. Their interactions with students are thoughtful and effective."

What do the results have in common?

Five practices run through the case studies, the signed letters and the commitments FocusedEDU makes to every partner. Credentialing comes before a candidate is presented, the school chooses from a shortlist, there is one partner per market, temp-to-perm comes at no cost, and the recruiting plan is built for the school.

  • Credentialing happens before you see a candidate. At Odyssey, each candidate was sourced, interviewed, credentialed and reference-checked before the shortlist. At Cesar Chavez and First Philadelphia, FocusedEDU handled the advertising, interviewing, credentialing and screening. Automated credentialing cuts hiring time in half while weeding out unqualified candidates before they ever reach your desk. In Dr. Weathington's words, the firm's "thorough screening process ensures that only the most qualified individuals are selected."
  • You choose from a shortlist. Cesar Chavez saw 4 qualified candidates per opening on average. First Philadelphia saw multiple vetted candidates per opening. FocusedEDU sources, interviews and credentials. You interview and choose, and you retain the hiring decision.
  • One partner per market. Your talent pipeline is yours alone. FocusedEDU won't take on a directly competing school or district in your area, so the educators recruited for you are never shared with a rival down the road. The number of your direct competitors FocusedEDU will staff is 0.
  • Temp-to-perm, at no cost. Evaluate a professional on the job before you commit to a permanent hire, at no additional cost to your school. Odyssey's CEO and Lotus School for Excellence's HR director each put that in a signed letter.
  • The recruiting plan is built for your school. Odyssey and IDEA each got digital advertising, information sessions held at the school and grassroots recruiting. At IDEA the campaign was built on the experiences of the contractors already placed there.

FocusedEDU was founded by a former K-12 educator who has stood at the front of the classroom. We hire the way you would.

How would this work for your district?

You send the opening, FocusedEDU recruits and screens for it, and you interview and choose. It takes 3 steps.

  1. Tell us what is open. Share the role, school, schedule, caseload and qualifications you need.
  2. Review the right fit. FocusedEDU recruits and screens for your requirements, coordinates interviews and shares candidates for your decision.
  3. Coordinate an approved start. FocusedEDU tracks required documentation and coordinates onboarding with your team. You retain the hiring decision.

FocusedEDU recruits special education teachers, paraprofessionals, substitutes, related-service providers and school-based behavioral support for K-12 schools and districts. Automated credentialing, background checks and documentation are handled before a candidate ever reaches you, so every professional presented is ready to work. With temp-to-perm, you evaluate first and hire permanently at no additional cost to your school.

On a 30-minute discovery call, we give you a realistic timeline for your specific need, walk through the letters that match your situation, and connect you with a school leader who has worked with us. The call is free and carries no obligation.

Send us the role, the school, the schedule, the caseload and the qualifications you need. Send a staffing request, or book a call and we will go through these results with you, school by school.
